body.statement: For the fixed binary family in \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\), the two models belong to the same \(\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A)\), have exact common summary \(1\to2\), \(2\to1\), \(2\to3\), no bidirected edges, the same strictly positive entire stationary observed law as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and separately identifiable refinement-specific effects, but \(P_{M_0}(O_{3,0}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(O_{1,-1}=0))=13/50\) and \(P_{M_1}(O_{3,0}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(O_{1,-1}=0))=1/2\).
body.justification: The pair is a complete direct fixed-alphabet rejection certificate with exact effects.
body.gap: It is one collision, not a grammar for all rejecting states.
body.consumer: It is the certified procedure's explicit failure regression test.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(A_t=O_{1,t}\), \(B_t=O_{2,t}\), and \(C_t=O_{3,t}\), and for \(s\in(0,1)\) define \(b_s(d)=s^d(1-s)^{1-d}\), \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  All variables are binary by \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\).  The two-sided structural solutions exist and are unique causal functions of the noise histories.  Indeed, model zero obeys
\[
 B_t=(R_t\wedge B_{t-1})\oplus U_t\oplus N_t,
\]
and model one obeys
\[
 A_t=(R'_t\wedge A_{t-1})\oplus U'_t\oplus N'_t.
\]
Whenever \(R_t=0\), respectively \(R'_t=0\), the right side forgets the preceding state.  Such reset times occur infinitely often backward almost surely because the reset indicators are independent with probability \(1/2\).  Starting at the most recent reset before \(t\) defines the state at \(t\), and any two causal solutions agree after that reset.  This construction commutes with integer time shifts.

In model zero, conditional on the complete observed past, \(U_t\) is an independent fair bit.  Hence, for \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_0}(A_t=a,B_t=b\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})
 &=P_{M_0}(A_t=a\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})P_{M_0}(N_t=a\oplus b)\\
 &=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
 \end{aligned}
\]
In model one, the same argument makes \(B_t\) conditionally fair and \(A_t=B_t\oplus N'_t\), so
\[
 P_{M_1}(A_t=a,B_t=b\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
\]
Thus in either model \((A_t,B_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) is an independent sequence with common mass
\[
 \pi(a,b)=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
\]
Moreover, in both models,
\[
 P(C_t=c\mid(A_s,B_s)_{s\in\mathbb Z},(C_s)_{s<t})=b_r(c\oplus B_{t-1}).
\]
Both observed processes therefore admit the same representation: draw the pairs \((A_t,B_t)\) independently with mass \(\pi\), draw \(E_t\) independently with success probability \(r\), and set \(C_t=B_{t-1}\oplus E_t\).  For a complete cylinder on an interval \([u,v]\), its probability is
\[
 \sum_{b_{u-1}\in\{0,1\}}\frac12
 \prod_{t=u}^{v}\pi(a_t,b_t)b_r(c_t\oplus b_{t-1}),
\]
with summation over any unspecified cells.  The formula is identical for both models and invariant under translating \([u,v]\).  Hence the laws agree on every cylinder, are strictly stationary, and, by the cylinder-uniqueness argument in \(\mathrm{lem:stationary\text{-}lift}\), agree as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).  Since \(q=1/5\) and \(r=1/10\), all factors are positive; marginalization then gives positivity of every finite cylinder.

The structural functions also verify exact graph membership.  In model zero, the active directed edges are \(B_{t-1}\to A_t\), \(A_t\to B_t\), and \(B_{t-1}\to C_t\).  In model one, they are \(A_{t-1}\to B_t\), \(B_t\to A_t\), and \(B_{t-1}\to C_t\).  Each instantaneous slice contains only one of \(A_t\to B_t\) and \(B_t\to A_t\), hence is acyclic.  All primitive noises are mutually independent, so no bidirected edge is present.  The equations are time homogeneous, and every directed lag is at most one.  Both exact summaries are consequently \(1\to2\), \(2\to1\), and \(2\to3\), with no bidirected edge.  Finite binary support, semi-Markovianity, stationarity, and positivity now give
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A).
\]

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0)\) in model zero,
\[
 B_{-1}=N_{-1},\qquad C_0=N_{-1}\oplus E_0.
\]
Independence yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_0}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 &=q(1-r)+(1-q)r\\
 &=q+r-2qr=\frac15+\frac1{10}-\frac2{50}=\frac{13}{50}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
In model one, \(A_{-1}\) is a child of the fair variable \(B_{-1}\), which is the only observed parent of \(C_0\).  Intervention on \(A_{-1}\) leaves \(B_{-1}\) fair, and therefore
\[
 P_{M_1}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 =\frac12(1-r)+\frac12r=\frac12.
\]
Each effect is separately identifiable in its known refinement.  In model zero it equals
\[
 \sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}P(C_0=1\mid B_{-1}=b)P(B_{-1}=b\mid A_{-1}=0),
\]
because the graph has no hidden common cause and its relevant directed path is \(A_{-1}\to B_{-1}\to C_0\).  In model one there is no directed path from \(A_{-1}\) to \(C_0\), so the effect is \(P(C_0=1)\).  Cylinder positivity makes both functionals well defined.  This proves the claimed fixed-alphabet, whole-law collision and its exact arithmetic.
